items.followUp: Which protocol is commonly used to send email?

rubric.why: Shows what the abbreviation FTP stands for.
rubric.description: Gives the full form of FTP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing File Transfer Protocol.

modelAnswer: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer files over a network.

items.followUp: How does a web server respond when a browser requests a webpage?

rubric.why: Shows that the browser contacts a server to obtain the requested page.
rubric.description: Explains the browser's request to the web server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the browser sends a request to the web server.

rubric.why: Shows that the browser processes and presents the page to the user.
rubric.description: Explains how the browser displays the webpage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the browser interprets the received page and displays it.

modelAnswer: The browser sends a request for a webpage to the web server, usually using its URL.
The server returns the webpage, and the browser interprets it and displays it on the screen.

items.followUp: What does a server do in the client-server model?

rubric.why: Identifies the client as a user device or computer in the model.
rubric.description: States that a client can be a computer or hardware device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the client as a computer or hardware device.

rubric.why: Recognizes that client can also refer to the program requesting a service.
rubric.description: States that a client can be software that requests a service.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying client software or a client program that requests services.

modelAnswer: In the client-server model, a client can be a computer (hardware) or a software program.
It requests data or services from a server.

items.followUp: Write the HTML tags used to make text bold.

rubric.why: Gives the correct opening and closing HTML tags for italic text.
rubric.description: Writes the italic tags in the correct order.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the opening tag and 1 mark for the closing tag.

modelAnswer: Use the HTML italic tag: italic text.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of a hyperlink on a webpage?

rubric.why: Identifies a hyperlink as an element that can be selected.
rubric.description: States that a hyperlink is clickable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a clickable link or element.

rubric.why: Explains that selecting the link takes the user to a destination.
rubric.description: States that a hyperlink leads to another page, document, or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid destination.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink is a clickable text or image on a webpage.
When clicked, it takes the user to another webpage, document, or location.

items.followUp: What is a domain name, and how does it help users access a website?

rubric.why: Explains that an IP address identifies a device on a network.
rubric.description: Defines an IP address as a unique network address or identifier.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its identification purpose.

rubric.why: Shows what the address identifies or helps locate.
rubric.description: States that it identifies a computer or device on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the address to a networked device.

rubric.why: Gives the standard IPv4 structure taught at this level.
rubric.description: Describes IPv4 as four numbers or four parts (32 bits).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the IPv4 structure.

rubric.why: Adds the IPv4 notation and/or range for its parts.
rubric.description: States that IPv4 parts are written in dotted decimal form and range from 0 to 255.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the dotted-decimal notation or valid part range.

modelAnswer: An IP address is a unique numerical address used to identify a computer or device on a network.
It helps data reach the correct device on the network.
An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and is divided into four parts called octets.
The octets are written in dotted-decimal form; each has a value from 0 to 255, for example, 192.168.1.1.

items.followUp: Why should passwords not include easily guessed personal information?

rubric.why: A longer password is harder to guess or crack.
rubric.description: Recommends using a sufficiently long password.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for recommending a long password.

rubric.why: Using different letter cases increases password variety.
rubric.description: Recommends a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the letter-case variety.

rubric.why: Numbers and symbols make passwords less predictable.
rubric.description: Recommends including numbers and special symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including numbers and/or symbols.

rubric.why: Avoiding predictable choices improves password security.
rubric.description: Advises avoiding personal details and common or easily guessed passwords.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid warning about predictable passwords.

modelAnswer: A good password should be long and difficult to guess.
It should contain a mixture of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols.
It should not contain personal information, common words, or easily guessed patterns.
Use a different password for each account and keep it secret.

items.followUp: Name two things that should be specified when describing a problem to be solved by a computer.

rubric.why: A well-defined problem makes clear what information is provided.
rubric.description: Identifies the required input as a characteristic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning clearly specified input.

rubric.why: A well-defined problem makes clear what result is required.
rubric.description: Identifies the expected output as a characteristic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning clearly specified output.

modelAnswer: A well-defined problem clearly specifies the input data and the required output.
Its requirements and conditions are stated clearly, without ambiguity.
